chapter: Fletcher Henderson, Ella Fitzgerald and the early 1940s
title: The Rhythm Club as the black musicians' exchange
summary: Black freelance musicians could find work every day at the Rhythm Club at 132nd and Lenox, which functioned like an exchange.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, what was it, the Rhythm Club?
Yeah, the Rhythm Club was right on 132nd and Lenox.
Did you used to hang out there?
Yes, yes. Well, in those days if a
musician was free lancing, black musicians could go up there and get a job every day of the week.
Yeah. If people wanted black musicians that's where they came to find them.
